items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: People like Berry Gordy. He was working in the factory and he started Motown.

ctx.x: They could read you see. There was always, at that particular time, it was required to read. Reading marches, classical stuff, and everybody was required to take private lessons then. I’m talking about the 40s and 50s. In other words in order to get into the band, there was a B band, an A band, you’d have a private teacher. That was a requirement. So then when you joined the band they would teach you, you could play these tunes. But there was no thing about learning to play the instrument you know. It was…

know. The people was making money and people was working you know. People buying homes and forming businesses and creating businesses. So the infrastructure and the environment was very ludicrous [lucrative?] — actually prolific back in those days you know. People used to come in from the south and as far as Poland to come and work in the factory. People like Berry Gordy. He was working in the factory and he started Motown. A lot of businesses started as a byproduct of the auto industry.
Was there a point that you said to yourself and maybe to your parents or your family that I think I’m going to make a career of this?
